name: a radar sweep finds signals in the dark
looks: Concentric rings glow around a single bright dot on a near-black field. A thin sweep rotates slowly around them, and small dots light up one at a time wherever it passes, scattered at different distances from the centre, a field of signals being found in real time.
build: Rings are static low-opacity circles; each signal dot fades/scales in the instant the rotating sweep's angle passes its seeded position, same mechanic as radar-scan-reveal; the sweep itself rotates linearly, no easing.
sound: A soft, continuous low sweep tone, a distinct ping each time a dot lights up.
prompt: Glow concentric rings around a bright central dot on a near-black field, then rotate a thin sweep slowly around them, lighting up small scattered dots one at a time exactly as it passes, so the viewer watches signals being found in real time rather than told about them.
